Circulation Γ —Loop length —

Small structures along the loop create higher spatial harmonics. Viscosity and heat transport change those structures; your note sets their playback frequency. Circulation is measured separately—the loop’s mean signal is removed from the audio.

The equations behind what you hear
∂u/∂t + (u · ∇)u = −∇p + ν∇²u − u/τ − B(θ − ⟨θ⟩)ey + f
∇ · u = 0
∂θ/∂t + u · ∇θ = κ∇²θ − θ/8 + Q

A unit square with periodic edges: flow leaving one side returns on the other. Velocity, pressure and temperature use dimensionless model units; screen y points downward. Notes add momentum and heat impulses. A pressure solve enforces incompressibility. Heat moves with the flow, diffuses, and relaxes toward zero with an 8-unit decay time.

The Reynolds number uses box length L = 1 and RMS speed; it is not a claim that turbulence is resolved. The 48 × 48 grid and semi-Lagrangian interpolation add numerical diffusion. These are approximate two-dimensional flows, with no free water surface or three-dimensional vortex stretching.

Pressure here is the incompressibility pressure, not an acoustic pressure wave. RHEO sonifies measured spatial structure using up to 32 harmonics. Musical pitch, envelope, tone shaping, normalization and effects are deliberate synthesis choices. Probe gains are 1 for velocity, 0.085 for vorticity and 1/0.7 for pressure before bounded normalization.

Methods: Stam, Stable Fluids (1999) ↗ · Fedkiw, Stam & Jensen, Visual Simulation of Smoke (2001) ↗. RHEO uses thermal buoyancy and a pressure projection, with no artificial vorticity-confinement force.

RHEO · RELEASE 1.1

RHEO 1.1 · A SMALL GUIDE

The flow is part of the instrument.

Project contact: AlirezaSamari on GitHub ↗ · alirexasamari@gmail.com

Enable audio, then hold A S D F G H J K for the white keys. W E T Y U play the black keys. Drag across the field to bend the timbre. Z / X change octave; hold Space for sustain or click Sustain to latch it. Esc releases all notes and clears effect tails.

Play demo starts a repeating phrase. Freeze holds the fluid evolution; you can still inject energy. Clear flow releases notes and empties the fluid. A longer Drag time lets earlier notes influence later ones for longer. Fluid voice at 100% removes the sine pitch anchor.

Save sound stores settings in this browser. Export/import carries a sound between devices as JSON. Settings restore automatically when available; the evolving fluid field itself is not saved.

Connect MIDI enables supported hardware inputs, with velocity, sustain (CC64), ±2 semitone pitch bend and mod-wheel vibrato (CC1). MIDI availability depends on the browser and its permissions. Computer keys and touch do not require MIDI.

Record captures the stereo synth output with effects for up to two minutes. Stop, listen to your take, then download the WAV. The last three takes stay on this page until it is closed or reloaded.

The Fluid Lab lets you seed a vortex pair, a periodic shear layer, or a thermal plume. Select a field view to see actual vorticity, pressure, temperature or speed. Heat and Cool tools add temperature impulses. Buoyancy converts temperature differences into motion. Listen to velocity, vorticity or pressure with a moving Lagrangian loop or a fixed Eulerian loop. The two probe plots show how a spatial signal becomes a musical spectrum.

Reference take · rendered with this same engine:

Inside the instrument

A 48 × 48 periodic MAC grid solves 2D incompressible flow with RK2 semi-Lagrangian advection, explicit momentum/thermal diffusion and a residual-controlled conjugate-gradient pressure solve. A bounded fixed-step clock targets 120 updates/s. Actual rate and dropped catch-up steps appear in Engine status.

Each note adds a discrete divergence-free vortex pair, a heat impulse, and a 96-point pickup loop. Moving loops follow the flow and are remeshed by arc length; fixed loops remain in space. Velocity, vorticity or pressure is sampled at uniform distances around the loop to form a waveform with up to 32 harmonics. An AudioWorklet scans smoothed tables at note frequency. Eight active voices have short extra fade tails during voice stealing. Pitch-bend headroom is included in the harmonic cutoff.

The fluid model drives musical synthesis; it does not simulate real acoustic water pressure. Numerical diffusion affects timbre, and time-varying modulation is not completely alias-free. This release runs in a browser or on localhost; it is not a VST/AU plug-in.

The numerical, DSP, message and file-format checks are automated. Interactive browser playback and physical MIDI hardware have not been verified in the build environment.
